messages:
emma_support: customer reporting intermittent 429s on the embeddings endpoint since last night. says only one of their projects trips but same API key used across projects. also hits are coming from a NATed egress IP from their infra.
max_sre: do we have any recent changes to the scoping precedence? last week we tweaked soft-burst allocation policies.
hari_eng: I didn't touch scoping heuristics, just the bucket refill tweak. but soft-burst now reserves a small per-org burst and a per-project fallback. could lead to surprises if IP limits also apply.
emma_support: repro steps from customer pasted below:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SK-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
They get 200 most of the time, then a 429 with headers: `x-rw-rl-limit: 6000`, `x-rw-rl-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-rl-reset: 21` and `x-rw-rl-scope: ip`.
max_sre: key detail: `x-rw-rl-scope: ip` means our NAT IP limit fired before key/project buckets. That matches the NATed egress assumption.
lee_support: customer insists only project A is seeing 429 while project B (same API key) is fine. how could ip-scope target just project A?
hari_eng: possible if their requests for project A have different `X-Forwarded-For` or are routed through a different NAT node. Or their app multiplexes projects across different hosts; one host saturated the IP bucket while the other didn't.
emma_support: customer provided proxy logs showing two upstream hosts: 10.1.5.12 (proj A) and 10.1.5.13 (proj B) both NAT through same public IP 34.120.10.2. but timestamps show bursts from 10.1.5.12 around the 429s.
max_sre: action items: (1) confirm our rate limiter associates by observed source IP (or forwarded header if config enabled), (2) check whether soft-burst reserves are being applied per org then stolen by ip-scope enforcement.
hari_eng: quick check: grep in ratelimiter logs for that public IP: `rg "34.120.10.2" /var/log/rate-limiter/*.log | tail -n 50`
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: ratelimiter@release-2026.04.13 (no config change to ip heuristics).
lee_support: customer asks if they can avoid this without infra changes. any quick mitigations?
hari_eng: short answers: (a) ask them to send distinct API keys per project — we can scope burst allowances per key which would isolate; (b) if they control proxy, spread outbound across multiple public IPs (eg. use multiple NAT gateways); (c) ask us to whitelist their public IP temporarily for higher burst (requires security review).
max_sre: also note `X-Forwarded-For` trust can be toggled for Private installs only. For hosted API we ignore XFF by default. If their proxy sets `X-Forwarded-For` but not from a VPC customer, it won't change attribution.
emma_support: customer tried rotating API key -> no change. they can't change NAT easily. requesting if we can change attribution to prefer API key over IP for soft-burst.
hari_eng: that's risky: prioritizing key over IP opens DOS vector where a single key can overwhelm others behind same IP. we could offer a conservative change: favor key only when `x-rw-auth-origin: project` present (we include origin metadata for dedicated/private).
max_sre: for this customer, immediate workaround: enable per-key quota on their account (support console toggle). that ensures our limiter charges against key bucket before deeming IP exhausted.
lee_support: can we do that now?
emma_support: customer ok with temporary toggle while they re-architecture.
max_sre: I can enable per-key quota flag for their org now. doing it will reflect in metrics within ~30s.
hari_eng: log to watch after toggle: `tail -f /var/log/rate-limiter/rl-analytics.log | rg "34.120.10.2|SK-REDACTED"`
deploy-bot: feature-flag update applied to org_4321: per_key_quota = true
max_sre: done. pinged customer — asked to repro and share a failing request id if it still happens.
emma_support: customer reports after toggle: throughput normalized for a few minutes then a single 429 at 1715432138 with `x-rw-rl-scope: key` and `x-rw-rl-remaining: 0`. they attached failing request id `req_6a7f3b`.
hari_eng: that indicates their key-level bucket now exhausted legitimately. we should review their token consumption pattern (batch size, embedding tokens per request).
emma_support: provided payloads: they batch ~50 inputs per request sometimes.
max_sre: embeddings cost scales with input tokens * batch size. for immediate relief suggest smaller batch size or increase quota/commit. also note long-tail retries can hammer refill. set client retry jitter and backoff.
lee_support: summarize next steps for customer: (1) temporary per-key quota enabled (done), (2) advise smaller batch sizes, (3) offer a temporary quota boost or whitelist if they need sustained burst, (4) docs link about attribution and NAT behavior.
hari_eng: also adding internal ticket to consider more granular hybrid scoping: prefer key when present but fold in IP as hard cap to prevent cross-org abuse.
emma_support: thanks all, I'll close after customer confirms no more 429s post-tune. :thumbsup:
